steps.title: Set up RNase‑free chilled environment
steps.instruction: Work with RNase‑free grade reagents, keep all cells, extracts, and fractions on ice or at 4 °C, snap‑freeze any unused reagents and store aliquots to avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Design and produce antigen
steps.instruction: Choose antigenic region(s) of the RBP: for low‑yield expressers select a 70‑80 aa segment with high antigenicity, surface probability and turn density; for high‑yield expressers use the full‑length protein. Clone the selected region into pMCH (MBP‑tag) for antigen production and into pGCH (GST‑tag) for antibody‑affinity resin preparation.

steps.title: Express and purify MBP‑fusion antigen
steps.instruction: Transform BL21(DE3) cells with the pMCH construct, grow to OD₆₀₀≈0.6, induce with 0.3 mM IPTG for 4 h at 30 °C, lyse cells and purify the MBP‑fusion protein by amylose affinity chromatography, eluting with competitive maltose according to NEB manual E8021S.

steps.title: Immunize host animal
steps.instruction: Inject the purified MBP‑fusion antigen into a rabbit or sheep to generate polyclonal antibodies.

steps.title: Prepare GST‑antigen affinity resin
steps.instruction: Express the GST‑tagged antigen in BL21(DE3), pass lysate through glutathione resin, cross‑link antigen on the resin with 14 mM DSS in DMF while rotating at 30 °C for 45 min. Wash resin with 10 × column volume of 50 mM glutathione (GSH) blocking buffer at ~22 °C, then with 5 × column volume of 0.1 M Glycine pH 2.5 followed by neutralization with 10 × column volume of 0.1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 at ~22 °C. Store sealed resin at 4 °C for up to 1 year. Set aside aliquots of input, flow‑through, pre‑DSS resin and post‑glycine resin for QC by anti‑GST western or Coomassie staining.

steps.title: Affinity‑purify antibody from serum
steps.instruction: Load 5 × column volume of crude serum onto the prepared GST‑resin, rotate gently for 10–14 h at 4 °C. Wash resin with 50 × column volume of PBS. Elute bound IgG sequentially with 12 × 50 % column volume of 0.1 M Glycine pH 2.5, each eluate collected into tubes containing 5 % column volume of 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 and immediately neutralized. Minimize exposure to acidic glycine. Assess eluates by western or Coomassie, pool peak fractions, and optionally concentrate using a 10 kDa MWCO centrifugal filter. Verify IgG integrity by Coomassie staining and quantitative immune‑depletion assays.

steps.title: Harvest cells and swell in hypotonic buffer
steps.instruction: Grow at least 10 mL packed cell volume (≈3 × 10⁹ cells). Harvest cells, wash with PBS, aspirate supernatant and measure PCV. Resuspend the packed cells in 5 × PCV of hypotonic Buffer A, gently pipette, and incubate on ice for exactly 10 min to allow swelling.

steps.title: Lyse cells and collect cytosolic S100 extract
steps.instruction: Spin the swollen cells at 250 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant (PCV typically increases from 40 mL to 55 mL). Resuspend the pellet in 2 × PCV of Buffer A and transfer to a Dounce homogenizer. Homogenize with a LOOSE pestle until ~90 % of cells stain positive with 0.2 % Trypan Blue (microscope verification). Spin homogenate at 25,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C and transfer the supernatant. Add 11.1 % (v/v) glycerol and 11.1 % (v/v) Buffer B to reconstitute the final S100 extract (final salt ≈280 mM). Re‑centrifuge if necessary to remove insoluble debris.

steps.title: Prepare high‑salt nuclear extract
steps.instruction: Aspirate any remaining supernatant from the nuclei pellet, add Buffer C (0.83 mL per 1 mL PCV) and swirl gently. Transfer to a homogenizer and homogenize nuclei with a few strokes using a LOOSE pestle. Pour the homogenate into a chilled beaker, then add 5 M NaCl drop‑wise while stirring until the final NaCl concentration reaches ~0.42 M (calculate volume using the provided equation). The suspension becomes viscous and gooey. Transfer to an ultracentrifugation tube (e.g., Ti‑45), rotate gently for 30 min at 4 °C, then ultracentrifuge at 40,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C. Collect the clear supernatant as the high‑salt nuclear extract and store aliquots.

steps.title: Extract DNase‑sensitive chromatin fraction
steps.instruction: Rinse the nuclear pellet with PBS twice, then resuspend in 1× DNase I digestion buffer (400 Kunitz U · mL⁻¹) proportional to cell number (use 200 Kunitz U per 1 × 10⁷ cells). Rotate for 30 min at 37 °C, spin at 21,000 × g for 1 min at room temperature, and collect the supernatant as the salt‑resistant, DNase‑sensitive chromatin‑bound fraction. Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Affinity‑purify endogenous RNPs
steps.instruction: Add 0.2 mM DTT, 200 µM PMSF, RNase inhibitor and protease‑inhibitor cocktail to all buffers. (Optional low‑salt route: dilute nuclear extract 3‑fold with 0.42× Buffer C to obtain ~140 mM NaCl.) Spin the nuclear extract at 21,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C and keep the cleared supernatant. Wash Protein A‑agarose beads twice with PBS, then block twice with nuclear buffer 420 + BSA (10 min rotation at 4 °C). Wash beads once with nuclear buffer 420 without BSA. Pre‑clear the extract by adding 60 µL of 50 % slurry Protein A beads per 1 mL extract, rotating 4 °C for 1 h. Pellet beads at 7,000 × g for 30 s at 4 °C and transfer the supernatant (pre‑cleared nuclear extract). Add 30 µg of the purified anti‑RBP antibody to 1 mL pre‑cleared extract, rotate 4 °C for 60 min. Add 60 µL of pre‑washed Protein A beads (50 % slurry) and rotate 4 °C for ≤4 h. Wash the beads four times with ~30 × bead‑volume of Lys450 buffer (or NP150 for salt‑sensitive complexes). Wash once with 1× direct assay buffer. Resuspend the RNP‑bound beads as a 50 % slurry in 1× direct assay buffer containing glycerol, snap‑freeze aliquots and store at –80 °C. Keep aliquots of input, pre‑cleared, depleted and IP fractions for QC by western/northern blot or activity assays.

steps.title: Optional competitive elution of bound RNP
steps.instruction: Elute the RNP from the antibody beads with 4 × bed‑volume of 0.6 µg · µL⁻¹ antigen peptide. Perform five sequential elutions at ~22 °C, 15 min each. Pool peak fractions and concentrate, if desired, using a 10 kDa centrifugal filter device.

steps.title: Prepare recombinant RBP and remove bound RNAs
steps.instruction: Express and purify recombinant RBP by affinity purification (e.g., from a CRISPR‑engineered epitope‑tagged cell line). Immobilize the purified RBP on its corresponding affinity resin. Resuspend the resin in Nuclear Buffer 420 + BSA containing 0.1 µg · µL⁻¹ RNase A and rotate 1 h at 4 °C to strip co‑purified RNAs (supernatant may be saved for proteomics). Wash the resin with 100 × bed‑volume of Lys450 buffer to remove residual RNase. Competitive elute the RBP with 1× direct assay buffer + glycerol (30 % glycerol) containing 0.25 µg · µL⁻¹ peptide complementary to the affinity tag.

steps.title: Reconstitute RBP with purified RNPs
steps.instruction: Mix the eluted RBP with the purified RNPs at the desired molar ratio in 1× direct assay buffer containing glycerol. Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 30 min. Proceed directly to enzymatic assays or the icSHAPE pipeline.
